name: Provider Auto Detect Plan
description: Bind saved provider connections to matching live local or remote runtimes so provider resolution becomes per-connection instead of global by provider kind.

userStories.title: Define runtime candidate and match types
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want explicit runtime candidate and runtime match types so provider resolution can move from global implicit runtime state to per-connection matching.
acceptanceCriteria: Add runtime candidate and runtime match types that carry source, status, local and remote URLs, model names, and match reasons.
Add connection-level resolution semantics so saved manual providers remain manual and legacy `workerUrlMode: "runtime"` can resolve through auto-detect behavior.
Saved `baseURL` and `manualWorkerUrls` remain the persisted source of truth and are not overwritten by detected runtime state.

userStories.title: Persist launcher runtime records
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want the Alvis and MN5 launchers to write local runtime records so the server can discover tunneled runtimes without special dev-server env injection.
acceptanceCriteria: `alvis:launch*` and `mn5:launch` write or refresh a local runtime metadata record with provider kind, model, local tunnel URLs, remote URLs, job id, and source cluster.
Launcher metadata is removed or marked stale when the runtime stops so dead jobs do not remain eligible for auto-adoption.
The runtime record format is stable enough for the server detector to load without SSHing into the scheduler on ordinary API requests.

userStories.title: Add low-frequency detector cache
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want runtime detection to be metadata-first and conservatively cached so Forska can discover live runtimes without aggressively pinging healthy models.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a server-side detector service that caches healthy runtime detection longer and backs off after failures instead of probing on a tight loop.
The detector loads launcher metadata and saved provider settings before attempting live probes.
Active runtime usage can refresh candidate freshness so normal judging traffic reduces extra probe traffic.

userStories.title: Probe saved local endpoints conservatively
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want the detector to probe only saved local provider endpoints so Forska can discover currently served models without scanning arbitrary ports.
acceptanceCriteria: Local detection only probes saved `baseURL` or saved worker URLs for supported local/runtime-backed providers.
The detector records reachable status and served model names from `/v1/models` or provider-native discovery for matching candidates.
Local probing remains demand-driven or stale-driven rather than continuous background polling.

userStories.title: Match saved providers to detected runtimes
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want saved provider connections to auto-adopt only one strong runtime match so manual settings remain explicit and ambiguous runtimes are never chosen silently.
acceptanceCriteria: Matching requires the same `providerKind` plus overlap on saved `baseURL` or saved `manualWorkerUrls` rather than provider kind alone.
Saved model ids can strengthen a candidate match but cannot override missing URL overlap by themselves.
The resolver returns `matched`, `manual-only`, `ambiguous`, or `unreachable` together with effective base URL, effective worker URLs, detected model names, and reasons.

userStories.title: Use matched runtime in provider test and sync
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want provider connection testing and model discovery to use the matched effective runtime so the Providers screen exercises the same resolved runtime that jobs will use.
acceptanceCriteria: Connection test uses the matched effective runtime when exactly one strong match exists and otherwise falls back to saved manual settings or reports ambiguity clearly.
Discovered-model listing and sync use the matched effective runtime and return the models currently served there.
Ambiguous or unreachable matches surface actionable errors instead of silently choosing a candidate.

userStories.title: Use matched runtime in judgments and runtime guard
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want judgment-job validation and send paths to resolve the matched provider runtime so remote tunneled models work through ordinary `dev:server` without global runtime env tricks.
acceptanceCriteria: The provider runtime model guard validates against the matched effective runtime for the saved provider connection instead of the old global-by-kind snapshot.
Judgment job creation and prompt send paths resolve their effective base URL and worker URLs from the matched provider connection runtime.
A saved manual Alvis or MN5 provider can pass runtime validation and start judgments through the matched tunneled runtime without `alvis:dev:server` or `mn5:dev:server`.

userStories.title: Expose runtime match state from the provider API
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want the provider connections API to return detection and match state so the UI and debugging flows can explain exactly which runtime a saved provider is using.
acceptanceCriteria: `/api/provider-connections` returns per-connection match status, effective runtime URLs, detected model names, source metadata, and human-readable reasons.
The response remains compatible for existing provider-connection consumers that still need saved connection data.
The API can distinguish `matched local`, `matched Alvis`, `matched MN5`, `manual-only`, `ambiguous`, and `unreachable` states without rewriting the saved provider record.

userStories.title: Show matched runtime status in the Providers UI
userStories.description: As a user, I want the Providers page to show which live runtime each saved provider matches so I can understand whether Forska will use my local server, tunneled cluster job, or only the saved manual settings.
acceptanceCriteria: The Providers UI shows per-connection states such as `matched local`, `matched Alvis`, `matched MN5`, `manual-only`, `ambiguous`, and `unreachable`.
The Providers UI shows the effective runtime URL or worker URLs together with detected served model names and match reasons.
Saved manual provider settings remain editable and visible without hidden rewriting when a runtime is matched.
Verify in browser: local manual provider matches a live local runtime
Verify in browser: manual Alvis or MN5 provider matches a live tunneled runtime
Verify in browser: ambiguous match stays non-adopted and visible
Verify in browser: creating a judgment job succeeds through the matched runtime

userStories.title: Demote global runtime env to compatibility mode
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want the old global `FORSKA_RUNTIME_*` flow to become a compatibility bridge so ordinary provider-aware runtime resolution works through `dev:server` without cluster-specific server modes.
acceptanceCriteria: Per-connection runtime matching becomes the primary resolution path and the global `FORSKA_RUNTIME_*` path remains only as a compatibility bridge.
Ordinary `bun run dev:server` can resolve matched local or remote manual providers without requiring special `*:dev:server` startup for provider-aware judging.
Legacy global-runtime behavior remains covered well enough to avoid regressions during the transition away from implicit provider-kind-wide matching.
